title: Switchyard after-hours handoff notes (draft)
body:
Quick context (TL;DR):
- Night shift covering: brief runbook for odd tail-latency spikes that started showing up at ~01:40 UTC on 2026-03-10.
- Symptoms: intermittent 95th/99th p99 latency spikes on hosted text-generation routes (models >= 7B) for requests with long prompt prefixes (historically > 1024 tokens). Error rate steady, but user-facing slow responses and occasional client timeouts (~1/min).
- Suspected cause: KV-cache growth + uneven eviction + fragmented GPU memory -> occasional kernel fallback causing long CPU path.
- Current state: system stable, spikes reproduced locally using load test; mitigation in place (traffic reroute to smaller model variant, temporary rate cap).

What I did (immediate actions):
1) Notified #sre-oncall and #platform-ops; posted brief summary + link to this doc.
2) Enabled temporary routing rule: traffic to /v1/generate for prod region eu-west -> fallback model x-redwood-6b-lite if request token_count > 1200. Implemented via routing config (console) _until 2026-03-12 06:00 UTC_.
3) Touched autoscaler to add one extra dedicated GPU slot for serving-runtime pool 'small-burst-eu' to soak potential backlog.
4) Added temporary token-level rate limit for anonymous keys: 25 requests/min for high-token routes.
5) Captured heap and GPU memory snapshots from the node that logged the slow kernels (node: runtime-eu-07). Saved in /mnt/logs/kv-spike-dumps/2026-03-10-01:48.{tar.gz}.

How to triage if it happens again (step-by-step):
- First 5 minutes (fast checks)
  - Check Grafana dashboards: "Serving /v1/generate latency (p50/p95/p99)" and "GPU kernel fallback rate".
  - Slack quick grep: search messages in #sre-oncall for recent deploys (keyword: release/model).
  - Run: ssh runtime-eu-07 and tail the runtime logs (last 5m):
      sudo journalctl -u redwood-serving -n 500 --no-pager | rg "kernel fallback|kv cache|evict"
  - Check GPU utilization: nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0 | rg "Used|Free" (on the pinned GPU).

- Deeper triage (10–30 minutes)
  - Dump KV cache stats via admin endpoint: curl -sS 'http://127.0.0.1:9080/admin/kv-cache/stats' | jq '.' and look for: total_entries, avg_entry_size, last_eviction_time.
  - If avg_entry_size >> baseline (baseline ~1.2KB), suspect anomaly in client prefix lengths -> find offending keys in request logs.
  - Check python/gRPC stack traces for runtime fallback: /var/log/redwood/stack-traces/ (files rotated daily).
  - Reproduce locally (if safe): use load test script loadtests/kv_repro.py with seed=20260310 – run against a canary runtime.

Immediate mitigations to apply (if problem persists):
- Option A (fast): extend routing rule (console) to keep >7b requests on 6b-lite until patch. Note: minor quality regression for edge cases.
- Option B (config): reduce max_contiguous_tokens default from 4096 -> 2048 for a 2-hour window (editing serving config and rolling to pool).
- Option C (surgical): force KV cache eviction on the afflicted node: curl -XPOST http://127.0.0.1:9080/admin/kv-cache/evict?percent=40 -> monitor latency. Use cautiously; evictions cause transient cold starts.
- Option D (scaling): add 2 more GPUs to the pool and temporarily increase batch concurrency; automations must be checked to avoid thrashing.

Commands cheatsheet (copy-paste friendly):
- Tail runtime logs: sudo journalctl -u redwood-serving -f --since "10 minutes ago"
- Check admin kv stats: curl -sS 'http://127.0.0.1:9080/admin/kv-cache/stats' | jq '.'
- Trigger eviction (40%): curl -XPOST 'http://127.0.0.1:9080/admin/kv-cache/evict?percent=40'
- GPU free memory: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free,memory.used --format=csv -i 0
- Re-route in console: console.redwood.ai -> Routing -> prod-eu -> add policy (condition: token_count > 1200) -> target: x-redwood-6b-lite

Signals to escalate (who to ping):
- If p99 stays elevated for >30 minutes after mitigations -> page SRE Escalation: @oncall-engineering (pager duty).
- If evidence of kernel regression (stack traces show new CUDA error strings) -> ping infra/serving-runtime (Marcus Li).
- If customer-facing errors/timeouts > 2% -> loop in support-eng and account-owners (Diego Alvarez).
- If mitigation rollouts (config/model reroute) need rollback -> contact release-engineering (release@redwood.ai).

Open questions / TODOs (follow-ups I want someone to pick up tomorrow):
- (PR) Add a per-key prefix-length histogram to the admin metrics so we can see which clients push huge prompts. Ticket: JIRA:SERV-8470 (priority: P2).
- (Investigation) Why eviction didn't trigger earlier: check eviction policy logs and whether eviction threshold JS config was accidentally doubled in last config PR. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood/runway/pull/3121.
- (Longer fix) Work with research to add a light-weight prefix compression step to reduce avg entry size (discuss design next week).

Notes to the next shift (practical):
- If you see increased tail latency, don't immediately restart whole node. Start with cache eviction and routing rule; restarting can create backpressure and bigger cold-start latencies.
- Keep the temporary routing rule in place until a reproducible fix is validated in canary and merged (expect ~6–12h).
- Leave a short message in #sre-oncall summarizing actions taken and link to this doc. Use the subject: "Switchyard: after-hours lat spikes — actions TL;DR".
- Log the start/end times of any temporary mitigations in the incident timeline (section below).

Incident timeline (template — fill in as you act):
- 2026-03-10 01:42 UTC — first user report via support; p99 jump to 2.8s (baseline 0.7s).
- 2026-03-10 01:48 UTC — collected dumps from runtime-eu-07 -> attached to ticket.
- 2026-03-10 01:55 UTC — routing rule applied: high-token -> x-redwood-6b-lite.
- 2026-03-10 02:05 UTC — p99 dropped to 1.1s; still spiking occasionally.
- 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC — increased small-burst-eu pool capacity by 1 GPU.
- 2026-03-12 05:48 UTC — follow-up: scheduled PR for histogram metrics.

Random notes / things I scribbled while debugging:
- Observed that one client showed consistent 4000+ token prefixes from EU region (client id masked in logs: client_xx_9). We should reach out via account-eng for guidance if we start to throttle.
- Found anomalous commit that changed eviction percent from 30 -> 60 (commit diff id: a1b2c3f) — might explain delayed eviction.
- Load test script used: infra/tools/loadtests/kv_spike_repro.sh (seed=42).

If you take over (next steps checklist):
- [ ] Post summary in #sre-oncall and tag @oncall-eng.
- [ ] Confirm routing rule end-time or extend if you're still seeing spikes.
- [ ] Create follow-up ticket for histogram metrics and link this doc.
- [ ] If you run eviction, watch for cold-start errors and increase retries on clients temporarily.
- [ ] Hand back with timeline + anything outstanding.

Personal signoff: I expect this to be a config/operational problem rather than a model regression, but keep an eye on new kernel errors. Leaving this as a lightweight, copyable runbook — please clean it up into Confluence if we decide this deserves a permanent runbook entry.

— Priya
(switchyard shift, 01:00–05:00 UTC)
